file name: kotlin-test-*.jar, kotlin-stdlib-*.jar, kotlin-reflect-*.jar, kotlin-stdlib-jdk8-*.jar CVE-2026-53914 is a build-time deserialization flaw in the Kotlin compiler / KAPT build-cache metadata (CWE-502), fixed in Kotlin 2.4.20. It is exploitable only by an attacker who can poison the local build cache (JetBrains rates it 6.7/medium: local, high privileges). The scanner matches it here via the broad cpe:2.3:a:jetbrains:kotlin CPE against any org.jetbrains.kotlin runtime artifact at the flagged version - none of which contain the vulnerable build-cache/KAPT code, and kotlin-test is test-scoped and not shipped to consumers. Remove this suppression once kotlin.version is bumped to 2.4.20+ (stable expected ~Sept 2026; 2.4.0 does NOT contain the fix).

file name: spring-boot-starter-mongodb-?.?.?.jar Same class as the springdata-mongo-* suppressions above: one of our own artifacts matched against cpe:/a:mongodb:mongodb purely on the name. Already covered for springdata-mongo-queue and springdata-mongo-distributed-fenced-lock; the starter was missed, so CVE-2014-8180 (a Red Hat Satellite 6 MongoDB auth bypass, nothing to do with a Java library) still surfaces wherever the starter is consumed rather than built - it shows up in the mongodb-inbox-outbox example.

file name: spring-boot-data-mongodb-4.?.?.jar Wrong artifact, not a stale version. These two CVEs are against org.springframework.data:spring-data-mongodb ("4.0.0 through 4.0.15" among other lines); the scanner matches them onto Spring Boot's own org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-data-mongodb, whose 4.0.x version numbers coincidentally fall in that range. The actual spring-data-mongodb we resolve is 5.0.6, which is outside the affected "5.0.0 through 5.0.5" range and therefore already patched - verify with `mvn dependency:tree` before removing this. Drop the suppression if the scanner ever learns to tell the two artifacts apart.
file name: spring-boot-data-mongodb-4.?.?.jar See the note on CVE-2026-41696 above - same artifact confusion, same reasoning.

file name: tomcat-embed-*-11.0.??.jar CVE-2026-66299 is uncontrolled resource consumption in Tomcat's WebSocket *chat example*, and the advisory itself says users who removed the examples web application are not affected. tomcat-embed-core is the embedded distribution and ships no examples webapp at all, so the vulnerable code is not present - the scanner matches purely on the apache:tomcat CPE version range. Scoped to the whole org.apache.tomcat.embed group, not just -core: the CPE matches every artifact in it, so naming one only moves the finding to the next sibling (it surfaced on tomcat-embed-websocket). The fix has since landed and been taken: the affected range is "from 11.0.1 up to (excluding) 11.0.25" and ${tomcat.version} is now 11.0.25, so this no longer matches anything. Kept rather than deleted because the reasoning above is about the artifact, not the version - tomcat-embed-core will never ship the examples webapp - so it stands if the CPE range is ever widened or the pin is rolled back. Delete it if you want the file to hold only live suppressions.

file name: opentelemetry-proto-*.jar, opentelemetry-semconv-*.jar Wrong language, not a stale version. Every CVE the scanner lands on these two is against a different OpenTelemetry *implementation* - CVE-2026-29181, CVE-2026-39882, CVE-2026-39883, CVE-2026-41178 and CVE-2026-24051 are OpenTelemetry-Go, CVE-2026-40894 is OpenTelemetry .NET, CVE-2026-44967 is OpenTelemetry-C++. They match only because cpe:2.3:a:opentelemetry:opentelemetry is written against the project rather than any one language binding, and these jars carry no language qualifier to distinguish them. Scoped to these two artifacts and no wider on purpose. opentelemetry-proto is generated protobuf message classes and opentelemetry-semconv is generated attribute-name constants: neither contains an exporter, a propagator, or any other executable OpenTelemetry logic, so a genuine finding cannot live in them and anything matched here is a false positive by construction. The real Java implementation (io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api / -sdk / -exporter-*) is deliberately NOT covered - a CVE against those would be ours to act on. Both arrive runtime-scope in the essentials-spring-examples demo only, via micrometer-registry-otlp and micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel; neither is part of the release.

file name: docker-java-transport-zerodep-*.jar/META-INF/maven/**/{httpclient5,httpcore5}/pom.xml Not on our classpath as a resolvable artifact - these are Apache HttpComponents copies shaded *into* docker-java-transport-zerodep ("zerodep" = it vendors its dependencies), and the scanner finds them by reading the embedded META-INF/maven pom.xml. Four CVEs land here: CVE-2026-71290 (9.1, TLS hostname verification) and CVE-2026-64607 against httpclient5 5.5.1, CVE-2026-54399 and CVE-2026-54428 against httpcore5 5.3.6. Two things follow, and both are why this is a suppression rather than a bump. A dependencyManagement pin on org.apache.httpcomponents.* is inert against a shaded copy - it would change the report's resolved version while the vendored bytecode stayed put, which is worse than doing nothing. And there is no upstream fix to take: docker-java-transport-zerodep 3.7.1 is the current release on Central, so no version of Testcontainers available today carries patched copies. Reachability: this transport exists to talk to the local Docker daemon over a unix socket or localhost for Testcontainers. The TLS hostname check and the HTTP/1.1 and HPACK parser limits all guard against a hostile remote peer, and the peer here is the developer's own dockerd. Test scope everywhere except foundation-test, which carries it at compile because it *is* the test-harness module. Re-check when docker-java publishes past 3.7.1: if its vendored httpclient5 moves past 5.5.1 and httpcore5 past 5.3.6, delete this block rather than updating it.

Second half of the docker-java-transport-zerodep block above - httpcore5 matches on a different CPE (apache:httpcomponents_core) than httpclient5, so it needs its own entry. Same artifact, same reasoning, same re-check trigger.
